## p102 A — ZITAG instruction to stop buying and loading

**Edition context:** ZITAG stop-orders and cancellation of procurement contracts.

**Related source pages:** [p103 B1](103.md#source-p103-b1), [p103 B2](103.md#source-p103-b2), [p103 D](103.md#source-p103-d), [p106 B](106.md#source-p106-b).

<a id="edition-cases-finance-zitag-purchase-orders-zitag-stop-orders-and-cancellation-of-procurement-contracts"></a>



**Source:** J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed pp102, 103 and 106, PDF page 105, 106 and 109. **Edition:** icekylinx
and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The [experiment](../experiments/zitag_purchase_orders/README.md)
contains the exact crops, literal coordinates, key provenance and repair
certificates.

Three 180-coordinate messages are almost identical copies of a short
stop-order. A separate two-part message on p103 deals with a request for
rubles, permits loading already paid consignments, orders cancellation
of other contracts and asks again for Westernhagen's prompt return.
The two orders have different scopes and are not merged into one text.

All five records use the unchanged published Nov1–3 square and ranks.
There are no geometry changes or newly assigned key cells.

<a id="source-p102-a"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-finance-zitag-purchase-orders-p102-a"></a>

### p102 A

The source heading is 1 November 1918; the receipt header says 2 November
without a time. It addresses the Prussian War Ministry representative
at Constantinople. All **180 coordinates** are observed. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXZITAGVOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSIVHERNXZITAG
```

</details>

The common readable candidate replaces source coordinates **29 G→X**
and **55 G→D**. Both replacements are observed in the other copies.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-zitag-purchase-orders-scope-and-attribution"></a>

### Scope and attribution

The short copies and B2 were already present as readable but unreviewed
repository screen candidates. B1 had a degraded candidate under the
wrong OCR length. Their prior bodies are frozen in the inputs file.
The source edition adds precise transcription, frame correction,
cross-copy evidence and reversible edits. A bounded check of the paper,
dissertation chapter and cached 55-comment thread located no explicit
discussion of these bodies; that does not establish first decipherment.

Together the five records contain **1,068 source slots**, **1,065 valid
coordinates** and **534 plaintext positions**. The raw models fix 531
positions; the explicit candidates fix all 534. Total cost is 14 observed
coordinate substitutions plus three printed-erasure fills. These are
edition coverage figures, not a count of newly solved cryptographic
symbols. Neither the stop-order nor the cancellation request proves
that the requested action was carried out.

```bash
python experiments/zitag_purchase_orders/verify.py --verify
python experiments/zitag_purchase_orders/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

Header: `NKJ v LP (8.11 p.m., November 2nd); 1/11 2210`, again with the

```text
FUERXZITAGVOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSICHERNXZITAG
```

| Source index | p102 A | p103 D | p106 B | Candidate |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 29 | G | X | G | X |
| 55 | G | D | D | D |

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

```text
FUERXZITAGXOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSICHERNXZITAG
```

**Readable German:**

> Für Zitag. Ohne Nummer. Nichts weiter kaufen und nichts weiter verladen. Alles möglichst sichern. Zitag.

Every candidate coordinate has an observed witness. This supports a
common original but does not prove which printed version is closest to

reading selected for its ordinary wording, not by majority vote.

The [complete p96 A source edition](096.md#edition-cases-finance-zitag-full-stop-order) independently
gives the same 87 nonseparator labels as this common stop-order body
without any source edit, and continues with a reporting instruction and
closing fields. Its 320-coordinate frame and separator placement differ
from these 180-coordinate copies, so this is plaintext-label corroboration,
not another vote at their source-coordinate indices.

It costs **10 observed-coordinate substitutions** and no fills. Its nine

### p103 B2

The second part advertises and prints **254 slots**. The first group is
`GG-VF`, source group `FCXGD` contains an invalid `C`, and a later group is
`AVG-G`. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
PARTIENVERLADENWERDENSOL?ENXSTORNIERETSAEMTLXA?DEREKONTRAKTE?EGENALLGEMEINERLAGEXERSUCHENWESTERNHAGENNOCHMALSSOFORTIGERUECKKEHR
```

</details>

The candidate fills those three printed erasures and changes no observed
coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
PARTIENVERLADENWERDENSOLLENXSTORNIERETSAEMTLXANDEREKONTRAKTEWEGENALLGEMEINERLAGEXERSUCHENWESTERNHAGENNOCHMALSSOFORTIGERUECKKEHR
```

Continuing B1 with editorial spacing:

**Readable German — continuation excerpt; the preceding words are outside this display:**

> … dass nur bereits bezahlte Partien verladen werden sollen. Stornieret sämtl. andere Kontrakte wegen allgemeiner Lage. Ersuchen Westernhagen nochmals sofortige Rückkehr.

The received form `STORNIERET` and the telegraphic wording of the final
request are preserved. `WESTERNHAGEN` is complete in the uncorrected
plaintext. The heading's different `WESTGRNHAGEN` form is kept literally,
and no particular person is identified from the name alone.

The final `SOFORTIGERUECKKEHR` is spaced as **sofortige Rückkehr**. No extra
`R` or connecting preposition is supplied to regularize the telegram's
grammar. The leading ellipsis marks words before this continuation excerpt,
not an unresolved plaintext position.

</details>

## Parallel Orient reports on South-Slav units

**Sources on this page:** p102 B1, p102 B2, p102 B3.

**Related source pages:** [p101 B2](101.md#source-p101-b2), [p101 C1](101.md#source-p101-c1).

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-parallel-orient-reports-on-south-slav-units"></a>



Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

Childs pp101–102 preserve closely related reports on South-Slav units near
Montenegro. The p102 report is an explicitly numbered three-part message.
The p101 material has a damaged first part and a matching detachment passage,
but some headers and wording differ. The edition preserves each physical
record instead of merging those differences.

<a id="source-p102-b1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p102-b1"></a>

### p102 B1

The [p102 B source](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p102_B.png)
prints an unavailable station pair, an unspecified reception time on
3 November, and `1227 ZON (1/11) 3 TLE`. Its first part is
`1 TL RICHI-208`, with 208 valid coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
ABTXFRXHEEREXGDXHXQUXSXMXNACHXORIENTBESICHTXVOM28X10XSINDSUEDXLAVISCHEXEINHEITENINMONTENEGROVORGERUECKTX
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
ABTXFRXHEEREXGDXHXQUXSXMXNACHXORIENTBERICHTXVOM28X10XSINDSUEDSLAVISCHEXEINHEITENINMONTENEGROVORGERUECKTX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Abt. Fr. Heere. G.D.H.Qu.S.M. Nach Orientbericht vom 28.10. sind suedslavische Einheiten in Montenegro vorgerueckt.

All 104 raw labels are fixed. Two observed substitutions, source 82 `X`→`V`
and 168 `V`→`A`, repair `SUEDXLAVISCHE` and `BESICHT`. No masks or geometry
changes are needed. Its recipient and administrative abbreviations differ
from p101 C1. `GDXHXQUXSXM` is punctuated as `G.D.H.Qu.S.M.` without expanding
its letters. The source date is the literal `28.10.`.

The shared subject makes the parallel useful, but `1225`/`1227`, the recipient
strings, the date evidence and `VON`/`IN` remain separate. This is not treated
as an exact re-encryption of the whole first part.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p102-b2"></a>

### p102 B2

The same p102 B header identifies `2 TL RICHI-200`. All 200 source
coordinates are valid.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEUSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETAIHEMENTXMRGTRXMNFZ2RGTRXKAVXMITGEBIRGSAR5L
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**


</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Wahrscheinlich das aus der suedslavischen Div. gebildete Detachement. 2 Rgtr. Inf. 2 Rgtr. Kav. mit Gebirgsartl.

The selected candidate uses six observed-coordinate substitutions and no
fills. The unchanged numeral `2` in p101 B2 supports an explicitly priced
repair of p102's raw `MRGTR` to `2RGTR`. The raw
`5` inside `AR5L` is repaired locally to `T`; no other numeral occurrence
or substitution-square entry changes.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-copy-agreement-and-extra-shared-word-repair"></a>

#### Copy agreement and extra shared-word repair

The two detachment records have **192 identical observed coordinates**,
**seven observed conflicts**, and **one complementary mask**. All
**128 minimum common streams** are preserved in the certificate. Their
aggregate substitution cost is seven, and they all retain the shared raw
word error `SUEUSLAVISCHEN`.

The chosen complete candidate costs three substitutions in p101 B2 and
six in p102 B2, for **nine combined substitutions**, plus the one p101 source
mask fill. The two operations above the minimum are the additional shared
source-44 change `A`→`G`, once in each copy, to obtain `SUEDSLAVISCHEN`.
Thus the fluent word is an additional priced repair; the copies do not
independently confirm it through an unchanged coordinate. The body wording,
unit labels and all individual conflicting values remain inspectable.

<a id="source-p102-b3"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p102-b3"></a>

### p102 B3

The third part is `3 TL RICHI-192`. It has 192 valid coordinates. The
[detail of `VGDGD`](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p102_B3_VGDGD.png)
shows a `D` at source 152, not an invalid `L`; no fill is charged or claimed
at that position.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
AUSXAGEDESXSERBISCHENOFFIZIERSDER3BATTR3FELDARTLRGTSXDONAUDIEXNXOX11NR2429VOM19X10XVODOHL11X0626
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
AUSSAGEDESXSERBISCHENOFFIZIERSDER3BATTR3FELDARTLRGTSXDONAUDIEXNXOX11NR2429VOM19X10XVODOHL11X0626
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Aussage des serbischen Offiziers der 3 Battr. 3 Feldartl. Rgts. Donaudie. N.O. 11 Nr. 2429 vom 19.10. VODOHL 11. 0626.

All 96 raw positions are fixed. One observed substitution, source 51
`X`→`V`, supplies `AUSSAGE` in place of `AUSXAGE`. The passage attributes
the report to a Serbian officer and gives the literal designations
`3 BATTR 3 FELDARTL RGTS`, followed by `DONAUDIE` and reference strings.
`DONAUDIE` is not silently converted to a different unit abbreviation, and
`VODOHL` remains unexpanded. The numbers `3`, `11`, `2429`, `19.10.` and
`0626` keep their exact encoded forms, including the leading zero.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-evidence-and-attribution"></a>

### Evidence and attribution

The published `Nov1-3` square and ranks retain the credit of **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The current source and arithmetic
review is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier unreviewed OCR
candidates are retained in the [prior-evidence snapshot](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/prior_evidence.json).
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed. The existing
[p100 challenge](100.md#edition-cases-p100) is a separate A message and keeps Armin's earlier
body credit; its status is unchanged.

[Literal rows, key and source images](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/inputs.json),
[recomputed domains and complete ledgers](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/certificates.json)
and [verification commands](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/README.md)
make the stated frames and repairs reproducible. The verifier also checks
that each readable passage preserves every non-`X` label in its cited stream.

### p101 C1

The [C1 source](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_D2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, received at `3.15 a.m., November 2nd`, origin
`1225 (1) 3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-190`. Its native 190-slot frame includes
32 printed dashes and a `C` at source 92. The fifth-row group is `GGGDA`,
with three visible `G` characters; its
[detail](../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_GGGDA.png)
prevents treating the second `G` as an additional mask.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
NO?MEC?E?SEN?NA?H?ORI?NTB?R?CHT?OM???10X?IOD?S?EDS?AVI??HEX?INH?I?EN5?NXM??TE8?GRO?V?RGE?UEC??X
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
NOXMACKENSENXNACHXORIENTBERICHTVOM??X10XSINDXSUEDSLAVISCHEXEINHEITENVONXMONTENEGROXVORGERUECKTX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> N.O. Mackensen. Nach Orientbericht vom ??.10. sind suedslavische Einheiten von Montenegro vorgerueckt.

The candidate has **93/95 fixed positions**, after five observed-coordinate
substitutions and 31 source-mask fills. The two date positions remain
unknown; the visible `10` is retained. Raw `5` in `5?N` and `8` in
`M??TE8?GRO` are locally priced word repairs toward `VON` and `MONTENEGRO`;
they do not assign any historical number. The beginning stays literal `NO`
(rendered `N.O.`), without changing it to a different headquarters abbreviation.
The word `EINHEITEN` fits the partially visible `?INH?I?EN` and is also
present in the related p102 B1 report.

The passage says that South-Slav units have advanced **from** Montenegro.
The corresponding p102 B1 text below says **in** Montenegro. The source
coordinates support this wording difference. The p102 date `28` is not
transferred into the two unresolved p101 positions.

## p102 C — Caucasus delegation asked whether to load the remaining Russian ammunition

**Edition context:** Caucasus ammunition: a request for loading instructions.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-caucasus-ammunition-loading-caucasus-ammunition-a-request-for-loading-instructions"></a>



The native p102 C frame asks whether ammunition still held at the reporting location should be loaded for the destination. The quantity is the literal **5280625** under the published Nov1–3 key. This source edition resolves three unknown labels in the earlier OCR reading; it uses no coordinate repair.

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Source: J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p102 (PDF page105). The Nov1–3 square and column ranks are the published key credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier OCR bodies are retained in [prior evidence](../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/prior_evidence.json); this is not a claim of first historical body recovery.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-caucasus-ammunition-loading-p102-c"></a>

```text
ZUDORTASRM1NR2078XLAGERNHIERNOCH5280625RUSSXISXDRAHTETOBMUNXNACHDORTVERLADENWERDENSOLLXMUVVERMITTLXSTELLESUEDOSTNR6829HITTMERXHPTMX
```

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-caucasus-ammunition-loading-readable-german"></a>

#### Readable German

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation only; umlauts display their literal two-letter equivalents:**

> Zu dort. A. S. R. M. 1 Nr. 2078. Lagern hier noch 5280625 russ. I. S. Drahtet, ob Mun. nach dort verladen werden soll. M. U. V. Vermittl. Stelle Südost Nr. 6829. Hittmer, Hptm.

`ASRM1`, `RUSSXIS`, and `MUV` are retained literally. The readable display separates their letters but does not expand these abbreviations or identify an ammunition type. It does not insert thousands separators into `5280625`. The references `2078` and `6829`, and the signature `HITTMER`, require no digit or letter repair. No external identity is assigned to Hittmer.

The earlier OCR had coordinate masks at source indices 3, 12 and 256. Native inspection reads `G`, `D` and `G` there. These restore the missing labels in `52?0625`, `WERDE?` and `H?TTMER`. They are corrections to the earlier OCR transcription, not historical ciphertext fills.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-caucasus-ammunition-loading-evidence-and-limits"></a>

#### Evidence and limits

The [input transcription](../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/inputs.json) preserves every source row, the published key and the exact readable display. The [certificate](../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/certificates.json) maps each plaintext position to its two source coordinates, preserves all numeral labels, and checks every non-`X` label in the displayed German. The [standalone verifier](../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/verify.py) re-encrypts the native plaintext to the full observed ciphertext. Its optional PDF mode also reproduces the source images exactly.
